slides.0.title: Reading the label
slides.0.subtitle: A label reflects both regulation and society
slides.1.title: Required and optional
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Required
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The appellation, "appellation d'origine garantie" or "contrôlée", a brand or cru name, the alcohol level, and the bottler's name and address
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Grapes
slides.1.highlights.1.content: At most two varieties for one appellation, and the wine must come exclusively from those named
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Other options
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Colour, vintage, label number and date, domaine bottling and provable awards
slides.1.content: Naming two varieties means those two are everything, stricter than a typical percentage rule.
slides.2.title: What may not appear
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Religion
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Any reference to religious terms, places or buildings is banned
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Château, Domaine and the like
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Words such as Coteau, Clos, Domaine, Château, Mont, Côte, Moulin and Tour are only for AOG or AOC wines from a real estate that has existed at least five years
slides.2.highlights.2.title: 1er cru
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Only for AOC wine from a specific terroir, of quality affirmed by tradition and classified by the national commission
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Vin de pays
slides.2.highlights.3.content: "Vin de pays" may not be used, nor geographical names other than appellations, such as a town, mountain or river
slides.2.content: The religion clause is the most Moroccan of all: wine may be sold, but never linked to faith.
slides.3.title: Primeur and Nouveau
slides.3.highlights.0.title: An optional qualifier
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Analytical limits
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Volatile acidity of at most 0.6 g/L (as sulphuric acid) and residual sugar of at most 2 g/L
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Link to label sessions
slides.3.highlights.2.content: This matches the Primeur label session in October and November
slides.3.content: With these three slides you can read most Moroccan labels.
slides.4.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge check
How many varieties may one AOG wine name at most?
C. Two, and the wine must come entirely from them
What is always banned on a label?
C. The colour of the wine
D. References to religious terms, places or buildings
Vintage and colour are optional; alcohol level is required.
How long must an estate have existed to use "Château"?
A. Five years, and the wine must be AOG or AOC
What is the residual sugar limit for primeur?
The volatile acidity limit is 0.6 g/L (as sulphuric acid).
